narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 34% probability of bad credit—roughly a one-in-three chance of repayment difficulty. Although that may sound below half, it crossed the bank’s risk cut-off for approval. The most influential factor was your checking-account balance in the 0–200 DM range, which pushed the decision toward bad credit; this balance range is less common among approved applicants at 18.4%, compared with 59.2% who have no checking account. The second factor, a used-car loan purpose, pushed toward good credit and was therefore a mitigating point; used-car requests represent 13.6% of approved cases. The third factor, your credit history showing past delays, also pushed toward good credit in this assessment, reducing rather than increasing the assessed risk, even though past delays appear in only 5.8% of approved cases. To improve your chances, ask the bank for the specific reasons and data used, correct any credit-history errors, strengthen your checking or savings balance, consider reducing the requested amount or shortening the 27-month term versus the 19-month average, and consider adding a guarantor before reapplying.
